title: Podcast EP362: An atomic layer in compute. A discussion of what can be built as graphene photonics scales with Cedric Huyghebaert - Semiwiki
gist: Black Semiconductor CTO Cedric Huyghebaert describes the difficulty and industry collaboration required to bring a 3-angstrom graphene layer into mainstream chip manufacturing, arguing that direct graphene-based photonic-CMOS integration could eliminate packaging and interconnect bottlenecks and enable new AI compute architectures.

insights.claim: Bringing a 3-angstrom layer of graphene into mainstream semiconductor manufacturing is a highly complex undertaking that requires broad industry collaboration across many tool vendors to reach the mainstream.
insights.speaker: Cedric Huyghebaert
insights.so_what: Highlights the manufacturing difficulty of atomic-layer graphene integration, a technology risk factor for the timeline to any commercial product.
insights.locator: who explains in detail the complexity of bringing a 3 angstrom layer

insights.claim: Black Semiconductor has made a substantial investment in building its own fab line specifically to deliver the cycles of learning needed to industrialize graphene integration.
insights.speaker: Cedric Huyghebaert
insights.so_what: A capital-intensity signal: building a dedicated fab line ahead of proven commercial scale is relevant for assessing the company's funding needs and runway risk.
insights.locator: Cedric describes Black Semiconductor's substantial investment

insights.claim: Graphene enables photonics to be interfaced directly onto any semiconductor chip using standard CMOS processes, eliminating complex packaging and electrical interconnects between electronic and photonic components.
insights.speaker: Cedric Huyghebaert
insights.so_what: If achievable at scale, this offers a potentially simpler, lower-cost alternative to the advanced-packaging-centric photonic integration approaches pursued by TSMC (COUPE) and Intel (EMIB/Foveros) — worth tracking as a dark-horse competing path.
insights.locator: He describes how photonics can be interfaced directly

insights.claim: By removing bandwidth bottlenecks through direct graphene-based photonic-CMOS integration, new computer architectures for next-generation high-performance compute and AI become possible.
insights.speaker: Cedric Huyghebaert
insights.so_what: An early-stage but potentially disruptive enabler for optical AI interconnect design, worth monitoring Black Semiconductor as a possible dark-horse competitor to established packaging-based photonics strategies.
insights.locator: By eliminating complex packaging and electrical interconnects

insights.claim: Cedric Huyghebaert brings over 25 years of experience at imec, where he built and led the scientific programs that first bridged graphene from lab-scale to wafer-scale industrial process, giving Black Semiconductor institutional knowledge no other commercial organization possesses.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A talent and IP moat claim relevant for evaluating Black Semiconductor's competitive differentiation and credibility in the graphene-photonics niche.
insights.locator: With a PhD in Physics from KU Leuven and over 25 years at imec
